disposition: Primary PARK2 donor fibroblast assays did not administer sumac to the patients or measure facial expression.
Open-field activity did not change significantly in mice given injected extract. The fruit-drink trial measured exercise pain and did not time Parkinson walking.
The human-cell Parkinson paper and the sumac locomotion mouse study did not measure dystonia after oral ground sumac.
An authenticated sumac fruit infusion was documented in a voice-remedy survey. Neither that survey nor a sumac-containing meal allergy case provides speech intelligibility scores.
Original culinary sumac allergy cases document acute reactions without reported visual hallucinations. They supply no comparison of hallucination frequency in Parkinson disease.
The Parkinson sumac study treated cells only. A meal timing study measured levodopa concentrations without isolating ground sumac or measuring daily OFF duration.

Sumac fruit extracts inhibited cholinesterases in vitro and injected preparations changed passive-avoidance behavior in rats. No study measured clinical attention after culinary sumac in Parkinson disease.

The clinical urinary diary study used fragrant sumach bark in a combination. Culinary sumac urinary evidence comes from microbial assays. Neither estimates Parkinson urgency frequency from ground spice.
The human drink study measured exercise pain, and zebrafish and cellular assays measured survival or cellular stress. The mouse open-field null result did not measure stride.

The culinary soup crossover measured aroma liking. The COVID-19 mixture trial measured joint smell and taste dysfunction and found no post-treatment difference between arms. A comparison of Parkinson olfactory impairment after consuming ground sumac remains open.
